lesson.title: Note Values and Rests
lesson.summary: The shape of a note tells how long it lasts; every note value has a rest of the same length.

section.title: Note values
section.p: The position of a note on the staff gives its pitch; its shape gives its length. The parts of a note are the notehead, which is hollow or filled, the stem, and the flags on the stem of the shortest notes.
Each note value lasts half as long as the one before it: one whole note equals two half notes, four quarter notes or eight eighth notes.

figure.staff: C5/w | C5/h C5/h | C5/q C5/q C5/q C5/q | C5/e C5/e C5/e C5/e C5/e C5/e C5/e C5/e |.
figure.caption: One whole note, two half notes, four quarter notes and eight eighth notes take the same time.

list.li: Whole note: a hollow notehead without a stem.
Half note: a hollow notehead with a stem.
Quarter note: a filled notehead with a stem.
Eighth note: a filled notehead with a stem and one flag.
Sixteenth note: a filled notehead with a stem and two flags.

section.p: Names differ between countries. British English, for example, calls these notes the semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver and semiquaver.

check.prompt: Which note value has a filled notehead and a stem but no flag?
check.explanation: A half note has a hollow notehead and an eighth note has a flag. A filled notehead with a plain stem is a quarter note.

section.title: Stems, flags and beams
section.p: Stems point up from notes below the middle line of the staff and down from notes above it. Notes on the middle line usually have a stem pointing down.

Eighth notes and shorter notes can be joined by beams instead of flags. A beam replaces one flag, so two beams mean sixteenth notes. Beams group the notes of one beat together so that the beat is easy to see.

figure.staff: G4/e A4/e B4/e C5/e | D5/s C5/s B4/s A4/s G4/q |.
figure.caption: Eighth notes beamed in pairs, then four sixteenth notes with two beams: each group fills one quarter-note beat.

section.p: Each further flag or beam halves the value again: a note with three flags is a 32nd note.

check.prompt: How many eighth notes last as long as one half note?
check.explanation: A half note equals two quarter notes, and each quarter note equals two eighth notes: two times two is four.

check.prompt: How many sixteenth notes fill one quarter-note beat?
check.explanation: A quarter note equals two eighth notes and each eighth note equals two sixteenth notes, so four sixteenth notes fill the beat.

section.title: Rests
section.p: A rest is a silence with a definite length. Every note value has a rest of the same length.

figure.staff: r/w | r/h r/h | r/q r/q r/q r/q | r/e r/e r/e r/e r/s r/s r/s r/s r/q |.
figure.caption: A whole rest, two half rests, four quarter rests, then eighth, sixteenth and quarter rests.

section.p: The whole rest and the half rest look alike. The whole rest hangs below the fourth line; the half rest sits on the middle line.
A whole rest also stands for a whole bar of silence in almost every time signature, as the next lesson explains.

callout.p: The whole rest hangs, the half rest sits.

check.prompt: A small filled rectangle hangs below the fourth line of the staff. Which rest is it?
check.explanation: The whole rest hangs below the fourth line. The half rest is the same shape but sits on the middle line, and the quarter rest is a zigzag sign.

section.title: Dots and ties
section.p: A dot after a note makes it half as long again. A dotted half note lasts a half note plus a quarter note; a dotted quarter note lasts a quarter note plus an eighth note. Rests can be dotted in the same way.

figure.caption: A dotted half note fills three beats; a dotted quarter note and an eighth note together fill two.

worked.title: How long is a dotted quarter note?

step.p: Find the value of the note without the dot. Counting in quarter-note beats, a quarter note lasts one beat.
Halve it: half of one beat is half a beat, the length of an eighth note.
Add the two: a dotted quarter note lasts one and a half beats, as long as three eighth notes.

figure.staff: *D5/q. C5/e B4/q | A4/e A4/e A4/e B4/e C5/q |.

section.p: A second dot adds half of what the first dot added: a double-dotted half note lasts a half note, a quarter note and an eighth note.
A tie is a curved line joining two notes of the same pitch. They are played as one note that lasts as long as both together. Ties carry a note over a bar line, where a dot cannot.

figure.caption: The tied C5 is sounded once and held for four beats, across the bar line.

section.p: A similar curve joining notes of different pitches is a slur. It is not a tie: it asks for the notes to be played smoothly connected.

check.prompt: A dotted half note lasts as long as how many quarter notes?
check.explanation: A half note lasts two quarter notes; the dot adds half of that, one more quarter note, so three in all.

check.prompt: A curved line joins two quarter notes on the same line of the staff. How are they played?
check.option: As one note held for two beats
As two notes, the second one shorter
check.explanation: A curve between two notes of the same pitch is a tie: the second note is not played again but adds its length to the first. A curve between different pitches would be a slur.

check.prompt: How many quarter-note beats does this bar last?

figure.description: One bar: a dotted quarter note, an eighth note and a half note.

check.explanation: The dotted quarter note lasts one and a half beats, the eighth note half a beat and the half note two beats: one and a half plus a half plus two is four.
